test_title: PYST 17: Selection Post (Higher Secondary Level) - Quant (Held On 28 Jun, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: maths
question: A shopkeeper keeps the marked price of his goods 50% more than the cost price. If he gives successive discounts of 5%, 10% and 20% on marked price, then what is his profit percentage?
solution:
**Given:**

Marked up price % = 50%

Discount (D₁) = 5% ; discount (D₂) = 10% ; discount (D₃) = 20%

**Formula used:**

Profit (P) = (SP - CP)

Profit% = (P × 100)/CP

**Calculation:**

Let the Cost price (CP) = Rs.100

Marked price (MP) = 100 × 150% = 150

After the first discount (D1) = 150 × (100 - 5)% = 150 × 95%

⇒ Rs.142.5

The 2nd discount (D2) = 142.5 × (100 - 10)% = 142.5 × 90%

⇒ Rs.128.25

After the 3rd discount (D3) = 128.25 × (100 - 20)%

⇒ 128.25 × 80% = Rs.102.6

Sot the selling price (S.P) = Rs.102.6

Profit (P) = (S.P - C.P)

⇒ (102.6 - 100) = Rs.2.6

Profit% = (P × 100)/C.P

⇒ (2.6 × 100)/100 

⇒ 26/10 = 13/5 = 2(3)/(5)%

**∴ The profit percentage**** is 2(3)/(5)%.**
